title: Impact of G7 Agreement for Global Minimum Corporate Tax Rate on Singapore's Ability to Attract MNCs
what_it_is: Impact of G7 Agreement for Global Minimum Corporate Tax Rate on Singapore's Ability to Attract MNCs

sections.label: Final parameters and compliance burden
sections.summary: Details on final parameters, design and implementation will be discussed in coming months, leaving uncertainty about impact on Singapore and affected sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Details on the final parameters, design and implementation will need to be discussed in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Therefore, there remains significant uncertainty in terms of the possible impact on Singapore and the sectors which will be most affected.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: When the details have been finalised, all jurisdictions will need to adjust their tax regimes to be compliant with the new rules, or cede tax revenue to other jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As we adjust our tax system, we will aim to minimise the compliance burden for businesses and ensure that Singapore continues to be an attractive place for business.

sections.label: US firms moving out risk
sections.summary: A question cites US Inland Revenue Service filings showing Singapore's share of US firms' foreign income taxed is second highest at about 7.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will there be a risk of existing firms moving out?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And I am referring to the United States (US) Inland Revenue Service filings which indicated that Singapore's share of US firms' foreign income taxed is second highest in the world at about 7.5% after Bermuda, and which indicates that US firms' here, for example, have about 165,136 people working for them, not to mention the cascading effects of some of these US firms in terms of subsidiary employment for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Risk exists today
sections.summary: The risk exists and exists today even.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The risk exists and they exist today even.

sections.label: Free Trade Agreements and opportunities
sections.summary: Several Free Trade Agreements have been entered into and new trade agreements are being sought in renewable energy, green and digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I have entered into several Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and we continue to sign FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We are looking at the various new opportunities for us to enter into new trade agreements including in areas such as renewable energy, green and digital economy.

sections.label: Keeping Singapore competitive against BEPS
sections.summary: These actions are needed to keep Singapore competitive, as BEPS 2.0 is one of many threats and Singapore cannot remain static.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We have to do all of these in order to keep Singapore competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: We must remember that BEPS 2.0 is one of many threats that could affect our competitiveness and we cannot remain static.
